name: Crimean Khanate, Major Slave Trading State
summary: The Crimean Khanate, established as a Golden Horde successor under Ottoman suzerainty, organizes systematic slave raids into Poland, Lithuania, and the emerging Muscovite state. Estimates suggest 1-3 million people are enslaved between 1450-1700, with the peak in the 15th-16th centuries. The slaves (mostly young people) are sold through the Crimean port of Kaffa to Ottoman buyers.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Crimean slave trade is one of the most consequential but underappreciated aspects of medieval Eastern European history; the demographic drain from annual raids stunts eastern Slavic population growth and forces continuous military investment in frontier defense (the Ukraine's etymology, 'borderland', reflects its perpetual frontier status); the trade makes the Crimean Khanate financially dependent on the Ottoman market, tying it to Ottoman political survival until Russian conquest (1783)
